transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you. I, um... well, I guess what finally pushed me to come in today, what really made me pick up the phone and actually make the appointment, is that my eating has just been completely all over the place lately. I mean, it’s like I don’t even know my own body’s schedule anymore. 

Some weeks, I’ll sit down at the table and I barely touch my dinner. I'll just push the food around my plate, and I have absolutely no desire to take a single bite, even if it's something I usually love making. It's just a complete lack of interest. But then—and this is the part that’s really been bothering me, honestly—other nights, it's the exact opposite. I’ll wait until the house is completely quiet, after everyone’s gone to bed and the lights are out, and I just stand there in the kitchen. I don't even sit down at the table. I just stand by the counter with the pantry door open, and I'm just eating handfuls of crackers and whatever sweets I can find... cookies, baking chips, just anything I can get my hands on. 

It's just so frustrating because there's no middle ground right now, you know? It's either nothing at all, or I'm up at two in the morning raiding the cupboards in the dark like I haven't eaten in days, and I just couldn't ignore it anymore. It's just so exhausting trying to figure out what my body actually wants.
After these late-night eating episodes, do you ever do anything to try to compensate or prevent weight gain, such as making yourself throw up, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively?

Oh, gosh, no. No, I don't do anything like that. I mean, don't get me wrong, the guilt afterward is just... it's really overwhelming. I'll be standing there looking at the empty cracker box or the cookie wrappers and I just think, 'Why did you just do that?' And I feel terrible about it, just mentally and physically heavy. But as far as actually making myself throw up? No, absolutely not. I have always hated throwing up, even when I'm actually sick with the flu or something, I fight it, so I could never bring myself to do that on purpose. And laxatives, no, I don't even keep those in the house. 

As for exercising... well, I probably *should* exercise more just in general, you know, for my health, but after one of those midnight episodes, I'm just so sluggish. I usually just trudge back to bed and lie there in the dark feeling uncomfortably full and just beating myself up over it. I don't go for a run or anything crazy like that. 

And I don't try to starve myself on purpose the next day either. I know I said earlier that sometimes I don't eat dinner, but that's really just because I genuinely have zero appetite on those days, not because I'm trying to, like, calculate calories or make up for the baking chips from the night before by fasting. It's not a conscious plan to restrict my food. So, yeah, I just sort of... sit with the uncomfortable feeling, as awful as it is, and I don't do any of those compensatory things you mentioned.
Aside from your eating habits, how has your mood been lately—have you been feeling down, depressed, or hopeless?

Well, honestly, yes. It's not just the eating, though I know I spent a lot of time talking about that. But my mood... it's been really difficult. I go through these stretches, these periods of time where everything just feels so incredibly heavy. It’s hard to even describe it properly, but it’s like the whole house just feels gray, you know? Like the color has just been drained out of everything, even on a sunny day. 

I’ll just sit there at the kitchen table, maybe with a cup of coffee that’s gone cold because I forgot to drink it, and I just feel completely empty inside. It’s this profound sense of nothingness, and it’s so strange because I’ll sit there trying to figure out *why* I feel that way. I'll run through the day in my head, trying to pinpoint what went wrong, but the thing is, nothing terrible has even happened. It’s not like I got bad news or had a fight with anyone. It’s just this unprovoked, heavy sadness that just sort of settles over me like a thick blanket. 

And it’s not just a fleeting feeling, either. It lingers. I’ll just sit there, looking out the window at the neighbor's yard or staring at the pattern on the tablecloth, and I just feel so down, so completely hopeless about everything, even the little things. It makes it so hard to get up and actually do anything, even just washing the dishes or sorting the mail. It all just feels monumental when that grayness sets in. So, yes, I definitely have been feeling very depressed and down lately, even when there's no logical reason for it.
Have you ever gone through a period of depression like this in the past, or is this the first time you've experienced it?

Oh, no, it's definitely not the first time. I really wish it was, I truly do, because then maybe it wouldn't feel so overwhelming, but... no. I've actually been thinking a lot about this, sitting there at the table like I mentioned earlier, just trying to make sense of the timeline of my own life. Because when you're in it, when you're trapped under that thick blanket of gray, time just sort of warps, you know? A Tuesday feels the same as a Saturday, a day feels like a week, and a week feels like a year. 

But I actually sat down the other day with my planner—I still buy physical planners even though I don't have much to put in them these days—just flipping back through the pages, trying to really track it. Because I wanted to be accurate when I finally came in to talk to somebody. And when I really look at it, when I add up all those stretches of time... those awful, heavy, gray periods where I just feel so incredibly guilty for no reason and I completely lose interest in literally everything I usually care about... it's a lot longer than I realized. 

If I piece it all together, all those stretches of time where I'm just hollowed out, they've added up to about seven months. Seven months of just... nothingness. It's actually really scary to say that out loud to you, to realize that nearly seven whole months of my life have just been swallowed up by this guilt and this complete lack of caring about anything. I mean, seven months is a long time, isn't it? You could grow an entire garden in that time, or learn to knit, or do something productive, but I've just been sitting there, staring at the wall or feeling terrible about myself. It just really puts it into perspective, how much of my life this is taking up, and I just keep wondering how I let it get to this point where it adds up to that much time, you know? It's just so much time lost.

And the sleep... that's the wildest part. Usually, when I'm in that gray place, I could sleep for twelve hours and still feel exhausted. But when this energy hits, I barely need to sleep at all. I'll go to bed at maybe 2:00 AM, and by 5:00 or 6:00 AM, I am wide awake. And I don't mean just awake, I mean I am *charged*. I can sleep three or four hours and wake up feeling completely refreshed, ready to just tackle the day before the sun is even up. I'll sit there in the dark, typing away on my laptop, drafting these long, complicated blog posts, or sketching out these elaborate garden projects that I absolutely have to start right that second. It's like I'm running on a completely different battery than everyone else, and I just don't feel tired at all, even though I know logically I should be exhausted on three hours of sleep. It's really quite something, how different it is from the depression.
